newsitem.title: USA: Fort Howard Q4 U.S. tissue revenues down.
newsitem.headline: Fort Howard Q4 U.S. tissue revenues down.

text.p: Fort Howard Corp said Tuesday that fourth-quarter U.S. tissue revenues fell from the same quarter of 1995 on slightly lower volume and lower selling prices stemming from industry-wide price cuts in the at-home tissue market in the first half of 1996.

Net sales of the paper company's non-U.S. operations rose for the fourth quarter versus a year ago on higher volume and favorable exchange rates at the United Kingdom facilities, offset by lower selling prices.
For the fourth quarter, Fort Howard's consolidated net sales fell to $384.4 million, compared with fourth quarter 1995 net sales of $415.3 million, the company said.

"This is due in part to lower domestic tissue revenues and in part to lower sales from the company's recovered fiber brokerage operations that experienced significantly lower prices for commodity wastepaper," Fort Howard said.

For the year, U.S. tissue sales rose 1.4 percent over the 1995 level. Net sales of the company's non-U.S. operations rose 8.2 percent on the year "due to an increase in net selling prices and higher volume of converted products at the company's United Kingdom facilities," Fort Howard said.

"Offsetting the increased sales at domestic and international tissue operations were lower net sales from the company's recovered fiber brokerage subsidiary because of significantly lower selling prices for commodity wastepaper," the company said.
For 1996, consolidated net sales were $1.58 billion, down 2.5 percent from 1995 net sales of $1.62 billion, it said.
Fort Howard makes and sells consumer tissue products for the U.S. and U.K. away-from-home and at-home markets.

The company reported net income per share before unusual and extraordinary items reached $0.52 for the fourth quarter ended December 31, up nearly 58 percent compared with net income per share of $0.33 in the same period of 1995.
"Very strong order flow for our at-home tissue products contributed significantly to our results throughout the year," said chief executive Michael Riordan.
